unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: A2 - THEME 8: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will design and write a project that explores the planets in our solar system, their satellites, and interesting facts about each planet. They will also focus on Earth as a planet and how it compares to others. Students will create scripts for different planetary explorers, astronomers, and scientists who are investigating and studying the solar system. Through role-playing and acting out these roles, they will simulate an interplanetary journey and share knowledge about each planet’s characteristics. The assignment will be evaluated using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the universe with its components such as planets and satellites in the solar system, facts about planets, the Earth as a planet'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what planets and satellites in the solar system, facts about planets, the Earth as a planet mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the universe'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''a passenger, a vehicle, an aircraft and so on'' and also some structures such as ''If we provide immediate support to homeless people, they will certainly survive the disaster'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''planets and satellites in the solar system, facts about planets, the Earth as a planet'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To help students plan and discuss a space-related project using target vocabulary and target grammar in English to improve their communication and critical thinking skills. Activity 1: Space Mission The teacher gives students a mission to plan a space project, such as exploring Mars for signs of life, reducing pollution on Earth, or building a shelter on the Moon. Students work in groups, choose a project, and use sentences with target grammar: Zero Conditional (e.g., ''If you travel to Mars, you need to wear a spacesuit''), Conditional 1 (e.g., ''If the weather keeps changing, we may have more natural disasters''), Unless (e.g., ''Unless we protect the environment, pollution will harm the planet''), and If Only (e.g., ''If only we could control the temperature on other planets''). Each group shares their plan, using target grammar and target vocabulary like Saturn, Moon, Gravity, Atmosphere, and Crater. Then, students write a short report. The teacher listens to the presentations, checks the reports, and gives feedback on what was done well and what can be improved. The teacher asks questions such as ''Why do astronauts need spacesuits on Mars?'' and ''If you could change one thing about the Moon, what would it be?'' The teacher also provides feedback to help students improve their grammar and vocabulary usage. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe planets and satellites in the solar system in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Fill in the Universe The teacher gives a worksheet with a short text including blanks and a word bank (Saturn, Moon, Gravity, Atmosphere, Crater). Each blank has a small picture as a clue. The text reads: ''The planet with the largest rings is _______ . The _______ is Earth’s satellite. _______ keeps objects on the ground. The _______ is a layer of gases around a planet. A _______ is a hole caused by an impact.'' Students read the text carefully, fill in the blanks using the word bank and pictures as visual aids, and then take turns reading their completed texts aloud. The teacher gives feedback by confirming correct answers, correcting mistakes, and explaining unclear points to help students improve their understanding. Next, the teacher asks shortanswer questions such as: ''Which planet is known for its rings? What is Earth’s natural satellite? What force keeps objects on the ground? What is a layer of gases around a planet called?''. Finally, the teacher provides constructive and supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
